epLog.choice: Black hoodie, black neck gaiter pulled up to the eyes, the Eagles cap Pop gave you turned backward. Nobody looks twice at a kid in a hoodie in Philly.
The fourth floor of Charles Library has air conditioning and a beanbag. Sleep.
Take the train down to Mifflin Street. Nonna said "come Sunday" ten days ago, and you never went. You can't put it off again.
Say nothing. Hold her hand. She already knows.
Go. Take the pizza. Whatever this is, Teddy said please.
Sit. Listen. "Why am I here, Teddy?"
Tell him what you know: the name Brannigan, the beds, the RA bounty. Everything Halcyon.
"After you, Your Highness." You're never going to stop.
Make her laugh. That's what you're for.
"I have to go. I can't tell you why. I'm sorry." Look at her when you say it.
The window. The woman, the baby, the boy. Get them out.
Don't climb. Think. Find another way down. The house next door. The roof.
"There was a fire. I went to help." The truth, or most of it. No more than that.
"I keep the closet door closed. Every night. Since I was a kid. Mikey told me there was a guy in there." Give her one of yours.
Carmen Torres. The bus. "I was too slow. A grandmother broke her hip because I was half a second too slow."
Lean in. Slowly. Leave her every chance to stop it.

recap.t: You moved into Cardone Hall, 9th floor. You carried a minifridge nobody asked you to carry.
At 11:51:04 on Saturday night, every clock in North Philadelphia stopped. You didn't.
You pulled a little boy named Jayden out from in front of the 16 bus. He called you "the cold man."
A nine-second video went viral. The internet calls you WAWA GUY.
A man across Broad Street put a finger to his lips. Then a bus passed, and he was gone.
You told Nik everything. He wants to be your guy in the chair.
You finally went to see Carmen Torres. She gave you a medal of Saint Jude, patron of lost causes.
Three people in Gritty masks robbed an armored truck at Broad & Girard. One of them could stop things just by touching them.
The Inquirer has a new name for you: the Broad Street Blur.
Since Saturday, nobody can see Femi Ojo. Except you.

almost_kiss.text: At 4:12 a.m. on the roof of Cardone Hall, you leaned in. She put her forehead against yours. She said, "Not like this." Neither of you moved until the sun came up.

assunta.text: Nonna's mother, Assunta DiNardo, "moved" once, in 1918, during the Liberty Loan parade. She pulled a child out from under a trolley. Nonna says it runs in the women of the family. Until you.
